'''FliperOS''' is a [[Linux distribution]] based on [[Ubuntu]] 24.04 LTS, for the [[x86-64]] architecture, aimed at [[arcade cabinet]]s with a 15 kHz [[cathode-ray tube]] (CRT) monitor. It combines a [[Linux kernel]] modified to generate the video modes of those monitors, the Switchres utility, arcade and console [[emulator]]s, game selection programs (''front-ends'') and a text-mode installation and configuration menu.<ref name="readme">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS |title=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref> The project follows the model of GroovyArcade, an [[Arch Linux]]-based distribution with the same purpose, from which it takes the kernel patches and the installation flow.<ref name="sources">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Sources.md |title=Sources |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

== History ==
Development started in September 2026, with a build system for the [[ISO image]], an installer modeled on GroovyArcade's and installation tests in a [[virtual machine]]. In that same month the base became Ubuntu 24.04. On 29 September, [[GNU GRUB|GRUB]] was replaced by the Limine boot loader, the installer was rewritten as the <code>fliperos-setup</code> program and the kernel moved to the 6.18 series. The first ISO, version 0.7, was published in October 2026, and versions 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 followed in the same month, with updates installed at boot without a new ISO.<ref name="commits">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/commits/main |title=Commit history |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

== Features ==

=== Video ===
Arcade monitors and standard-definition CRT televisions work with a horizontal scan rate close to 15 kHz, about half of that used by the [[Video Graphics Array|VGA]] standard, and current operating systems don't offer those video modes by default. FliperOS uses the Linux 6.18 kernel with the 15 kHz patch set maintained by D0023R, the same as GroovyArcade's <code>linux-15khz</code> package, compiled with the kernel configuration of Ubuntu 24.04.<ref name="kernel">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Kernel-15-kHz.md |title=15 kHz kernel |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="d0023r">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/D0023R/linux_kernel_15khz |title=linux_kernel_15khz |author=D0023R |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

The boot menu has entries for 15, 25 and 31 kHz monitors, for [[Liquid-crystal display|LCD]] monitors, for [[NTSC]] and [[PAL]] televisions and for [[Intel]] and [[Nvidia]] graphics cards, which use wider modes (''super resolutions''). With no input, the 15 kHz entry is chosen after 30 seconds, because a 31 kHz signal can damage a monitor that only accepts 15 kHz.<ref name="install">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Install.md |title=Install |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

Switchres computes the video modes within the frequency ranges of the chosen monitor and generates the identification data (EDID) for each supported monitor model.<ref name="kernel" /><ref name="switchres">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/antonioginer/switchres |title=Switchres |author=Antonio Giner |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref> GroovyMAME and [[RetroArch]] switch modes on every game, to the resolution and refresh rate of the original system. The other emulators open in 240-line progressive modes on 15 kHz monitors, which avoids the flicker of the 480-line interlaced mode.<ref name="emulators">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Emulators.md |title=Emulators |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

=== Installation and configuration ===
The ISO image is only used to install the system. It is hybrid, boots through [[BIOS]] or [[UEFI]] and uses the Limine loader. On startup, the system enables one video output at a time and announces the test through [[speech synthesis]], so that the user confirms which output the monitor is connected to; the procedure was ported from GroovyArcade. Then come the choice of monitor type and the installation to disk.<ref name="install" />

Those screens belong to <code>fliperos-setup</code>, written in [[Bash (Unix shell)|Bash]] with the Gum tool, with English text and designed for 640×480 interlaced (80 columns by 30 lines). On the installed system, the same program is the menu that appears when the front-end is closed. It configures video (monitor, orientation, resolution and picture geometry), audio, network, the default front-end and system updates, and can be operated with the cabinet's controls.<ref name="installed">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Installed-system.md |title=Installed system |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

Each emulator opens in the video mode intended for the configured monitor type.<ref name="emulators" /> The front-ends are Attract-Mode Plus, EmulationStation (ES-DE) and Pegasus, distributed as <code>.deb</code> packages from the project's own APT repository, included in the image; the last two get themes made for 240-line screens.<ref name="frontends">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Frontends.md |title=Frontends |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref> The Fightcade 2 online play client can be downloaded from the configuration menu.<ref name="fightcade">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Fightcade-2.md |title=Fightcade 2 |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref> The [[LXDE]] desktop environment gives access to the emulators, to [[Steam (service)|Steam]] and to a [[Flatpak]] app store.<ref name="desktop">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Desktop.md |title=Desktop and theme |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

=== Tools ===
The configuration menu includes:
* a ''scraper'', which fetches covers, videos and descriptions of the games for the front-ends;<ref name="scraper">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Scraper.md |title=Scraper |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>
* a filter for MAME ROM collections, by category, number of players and control type, and another that copies the disk images (CHD) of the games kept;<ref name="roms">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/ROMs.md |title=ROMs, BIOS and artwork |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>
* button mapping for each player, calibration of light guns and wheels and the use of joysticks connected to the [[parallel port]];<ref name="controls">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Controls.md |title=Controls |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>
* two latency modes, one for any computer and another, with less delay, for recent processors.<ref name="latency">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Latency.md |title=Latency |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

The ROM, BIOS, artwork and configuration folders are accessible over the local network through [[Samba (software)|Samba]], and the system accepts remote access through [[Secure Shell|SSH]].<ref name="architecture">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Architecture.md |title=Architecture |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>

== Development ==
The image is built in a [[Docker (software)|Docker]] container. Automated tests in [[Python (programming language)|Python]] check the logic of the configuration program and the contents of the image, and the installation is exercised in [[QEMU]] virtual machines, through BIOS and UEFI. Components that Ubuntu 24.04 doesn't offer, such as Limine, Gum, GroovyMAME and PCSX2, are downloaded in pinned versions, verified by [[Cryptographic hash function|hash]].<ref name="build">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/juniorterin/fliperOS/blob/main/docs/wiki/Build-and-tests.md |title=Build and tests |work=FliperOS |publisher=GitHub |language=en |access-date=6 October 2026}}</ref>
